data.title: HOOD stock falls 8.5% as Robinhood’s crypto revenue weakness draws attention
data.description:
The Robinhood Markets HOOD stock fell 8.55% to $83.76 in early trading on October 30, extending its October decline. Its price opened well below the price it closed at on Thursday as cryptocurrency markets faced fresh uncertainty surrounding Binance’s security incident.

The selling comes days after Robinhood reported a 55% annual drop in quarterly crypto revenue. Its latest results offer a useful measure of its exposure as investors assess the fallout across crypto markets.

Crypto revenue falls despite record company sales

The Robinhood third-quarter results that was published on October 27, showed that crypto revenue was $120 million. This amount made up about 8.4% of the total revenue.

The total revenue reached a record $1.424 billion, up 12% year over year. Options brought in $399 million, while event contracts brought in $173 million.

Those businesses helped to make up for the crypto decline. But net income fell 14% to $476 million, and earnings per share dropped 16% to $0.51.

Binance adds uncertainty to the backdrop

In an October 30 update, Binance estimated that the impact of its security incident was about $6.3 billion. But it said that about $3 billion in affected assets had been frozen.

The exchange temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals during security checks, and it said it would cover losses with its emergency reserve.

For Robinhood, the question is how customers respond to the event.

As could be seen on the chart, HOOD was already declining before the security reports.

HOOD loses ground below $90

At the time of this writing, HOOD was trading at around $83.76.

Its price opened at $85.21, compared with $91.59, where it closed the previous day, and it dropped to the $82.34 price level before it recovered a bit.

A look at its trend over the past week showed that it has declined from its September highs above $120. The repeated declines it has seen in October had already brought its price below $100 ahead of Friday’s opening drop.

It remains to be seen if HOOD can hold above the $82.34 price level it dropped to during the session. Around $80 provides another nearby reference area. If it recovers toward the $89–$92 price area, it would return its price to the range it occupied in the last sessions.

Final Summary

HOOD dropped by 8.55% to trade at $83.76 on October 30, extending an earlier decline.

Robinhood’s quarterly crypto revenue fell by 55%, while other businesses supported record total revenue.

data.title: Kraken outage affects Spot and derivatives trading – Here’s what happened
data.description:
Kraken, one of the world’s major cryptocurrency exchanges, experienced a temporary technical disruption on the 30th of October 2026, affecting both spot and derivatives trading.

According to Kraken’s status dashboard, the issue began at 02:42 UTC and prevented some users from connecting to the platform and successfully submitting orders.

What happened to Kraken?

The disruption affected Kraken’s website and mobile application, along with its REST, WebSocket, and FIX APIs. For those unaware, these interfaces allow retail traders, institutional clients, and automated trading systems to access market data, connect to the exchange, and execute trades.

In simple words, this disruption might have caused difficulties for users trying to log in to their accounts, access trading services, place buy or sell orders, or execute trades through automated systems.

However, Kraken confirmed that the incident was resolved at 03:42 UTC, approximately one hour after it was first reported. But what is more important here is that this disruption did not indicate a security breach or loss of customer funds. In fact, it was more of a connectivity and order-processing issue.

Kraken’s demand remains uninterrupted

This follows the exchange witnessing growing demand for round-the-clock trading through its xStocks platform, which offers tokenized versions of traditional stocks.

This is because now more than 50% of xStocks trading volume now takes place outside conventional stock market hours. In other words, investors are increasingly looking for the flexibility to trade beyond standard exchange timings.

Additionally, Kraken has also expanded its xStocks offerings to over 1,000 listings since last week, broadening access to tokenized equities for millions of users worldwide.

Notably, AMBCrypto’s recent report suggested that Kraken was in a spotlight back on the 24th of October. On that day, Kraken co-CEO Arjun Sethi had apologized for emails sent to Monero [XMR] buyers requesting personal information, including employment details, proof of income, bank statements, and intended use of withdrawn funds.

Crypto hacks are on the rise

Like Kraken, Binance too announced plans to resume withdrawals within 48 hours following a temporary suspension for security checks after a reported $6.3 billion hack.

Still, according to DeFiLlama data, the cryptocurrency industry has witnessed a sharp rise in security incidents in 2026, with 322 confirmed hacks recorded so far, already more than double the total reported in 2025.

In fact, threats also remained active recently, with 12 confirmed hacks reported in just the past seven days, highlighting the persistent vulnerability of the crypto ecosystem to cyberattacks.

Final Summary

  • The disruption affected Kraken’s website and mobile application, along with its REST, WebSocket, and FIX APIs.
  • Kraken confirmed that the incident was resolved at 03:42 UTC, approximately one hour after it was first reported.

data.title: XRP Ledger to tighten permissioned token rules to attract institutional players
data.description:
XRP Ledger plans to tighten rules on who can hold permissioned, regulated tokens such as stablecoins or tokenized stocks. In an upgrade named fixCleanup3_5_0, which bundles four proposals, XRP Ledger intends to remove loopholes that currently allow unapproved users to hold regulated assets without issuer approval. 

For some tokenized stocks, issuers want to screen whoever is buying their tokens for compliance checks, including anti-money laundering (AML) and manipulation risks. As such, a permissioned environment allows issuers to run identity checks.

Until now, XRP Ledger has had ways to bypass this, which can derail onboarding of institutional players leveraging tokenized stocks and other regulated assets on the network. This is part of the chain’s push to advance and position itself for the tokenization boom. 

What’s next for the XRP Ledger proposal

The proposals were pushed out earlier this week. At the time of writing, the upgrade was yet to be merged into the main software, the next stage for validator consensus and potential adoption into the mainnet network. 

To advance to the next phase, the upgrade must get 80% validator support, or about 29 out of 35 trusted validators, for two weeks. 

Since the AI-flagged decade-old $90B risk to the network in September, the team has been actively scanning for flaws and vulnerabilities as part of continued hardening of the protocol. The advanced AI models have also elevated security risks to blockchains and digital systems. 

According to the XRP Ledger Foundation, the recent upgrade proposal is part of routine hardening of the protocol and not related to any security incident. 

So, will the proposal improve XRP Ledger ratings in the tokenization race?

XRP Ledger’s tokenized stocks traction

According to the RWA dashboard, XRP Ledger is the 10th largest network with $642.5M in tokenized assets. This is slightly below Base, which holds $650M of tokenized assets and ranks 9th. 

Interestingly, among the top 10, Base and XRP Ledger saw the largest growth in tokenized assets in the last 30 days. XRP Ledger’s value grew by 28% while Base’s traction increased by 69%. 

Overall, XRP Ledger is seeing traction on the tokenization front and wants to improve the underlying tech to advance the segment while ensuring compliance guardrails for institutional players. 

Final Summary

  • XRP Ledger is eyeing an upgrade to restrict unauthorized users from holding regulated tokenized assets and stablecoins. 
  • Network is ranked 10th in tokenized assets value with $642.5M, following a growth of 28% in October.

data.title: Curve DAO loses $0.30 support – Why CRV faces further downside risks
data.description:
Curve DAO [CRV] recorded a sharp decline of 17.08% in the last 24 hours at press time, continuing to extend its recent decline as selling pressure intensified. Meanwhile, Spot trading volume surged 182% to $94.49 million, highlighting increased market participation during the sell-off. 

The rapid volume increase along with the declining prices together pointed to aggressive selling as opposed to renewed buying interest. Additionally, the derivatives analytics also revealed another concerning development as market participants reduced their exposure.

Notably, the decline also coincided with a broader crypto market crash, as the Fear and Greed Index fell to 38, reflecting growing investor fear.

Derivatives surge, but traders abandon CRV positions

The trading volume on CRV derivatives rose 126.53% to $221.82 million as of writing, reflecting increased volatility in the Futures markets. 

Despite increased trading, Open Interest (OI), however, declined 19.23% to $110.77 million,  suggesting a considerable decrease in active positions. These contrasting figures implied investors closed their positions instead of committing fresh capital to the market.

Generally, declining OI during a sudden price decline usually points toward position unwinding and potential liquidations. Such developments often tend to go hand-in-hand with periods of market uncertainty as leveraged traders exit the market. 

Exchange reserves shrink despite CRV’s steep decline

At the time of writing, the token’s Exchange Reserves fell 15.58% to $120.9 million in 24 hours, highlighting a significant reduction in exchange-held token value.

However, it is also worth noting that the reserve decline also reflected CRV’s falling price, which limits conclusions about actual token withdrawals. On the other hand, the Spot Netflows, meanwhile, remained predominantly negative, with October 30 recording roughly $218,990 in net outflows.

Typically, continued negative netflows imply reduced immediate selling availability as traders transfer tokens away from exchanges.

Despite these withdrawals, however, CRV’s price continued declining, suggesting that existing selling pressure had overwhelmed potential accumulation. This divergence raised questions on whether the reduced exchange supply could eventually be of help in stabilizing CRV price. 

Can CRV defend its next critical support?

CRV’s technical structure  on the daily chart confirmed a breakdown below $0.30, a region that previously supported several price recoveries. The bears pushed prices toward $0.2739 following the breakdown, bringing the next major support at $0.2372 into the spotlight.

Furthermore, the RSI indicator dropped to 30.24 as of writing, nearing the oversold territory and reflecting intense bearish pressure. Besides, the indicator’s position below its moving average further highlighted the fading buying strength.

The MACD indicator validated the bearish outlook, with its line falling to below the signal line, and the negative histogram expanding to -0.0030.

Ultimately, CRV remained vulnerable after losing the $0.30 support zone, while the declining Open Interest and bearish indicators strengthened the downside risks. 

Even though the exchange outflows offered potential relief, the bears still retained control, and failure to recover the $0.30 support could expose CRV to further losses toward $0.2372.

Final Summary

  • CRV’s 17% crash coincided with falling Open Interest and persistent market fear.
  • CRV could extend losses toward $0.2372 unless buyers reclaim the $0.30 level.

data.title: Binance to resume withdrawals within 48 hours after $6.3B hack
data.description:
Binance plans to allow withdrawals in 48 hours after a precautionary pause to conduct security checks following the recent hack. In the exchange’s latest service update, Yi He, Co-Founder and Co-CEO of the exchange, said, 

Deposits remain unaffected and continue to operate as normal. Our team is currently working on enhancements to the withdrawal service and related address controls. We expect to begin resuming withdrawal services in the next 48 hours.

The hack began at around 20:20 UTC on Thursday, 29th October, targeting Binance’s primary Ethereum hot wallet.

About 2 hours later (22:30 UTC), Binance acknowledged the exploit and issued the first statement of a potential attack. It suspended all deposits and withdrawals and opened investigations. 

Binance hack update: Nearly $3B stolen funds frozen

In a follow-up, the world’s largest crypto exchange said estimated stolen funds were about $6.3B. This was at 02:25 AM UTC on Friday, 30th October 2026. That’s about 3 hours after the initial preliminary investigation announcement. 

The $6.3B figure makes the Binance hack the largest ever in crypto history. The attacker drained Binance hot wallets across 10 chains. 

On Ethereum, the attacker siphoned $3.74B worth of crypto assets. On the Bitcoin network, the attacker stole 18,270.2 BTC worth $1.47B. On TRON, the hacker moved $612.7M USDT and 46.4M TRX (total $627M). Solana, Arbitrum, and Avalanche recorded $96M, $32M and $24M drains, respectively. 

In fact, the Ethereum and Bitcoin drains dominated 83% of the $6.3B heist.

Industry partners, including Tether, Circle, Ripple, Paxos, Arbitrum, World Liberty Financials, and Binance itself, have frozen about $2.8B already. That’s nearly half of the heist, most stablecoins with freezing features. 

However, the attacker can still move BTC and ETH assets, worth about $3.27B, according to on-chain and security analyst Dickson Wu.  

According to Web3 security investigator Zachary Wolk (popularly known as ZachXBT) and Chainalysis, North Korea’s TraderTraitor was behind the hack, citing commingling of Binance’s stolen funds with Bitget’s $388M exploit address.  

For its part, Binance traced the exploit to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop. This allowed TraderTraitor to gain access to the exchange’s internal infrastructure and sign off on transfers.

The exchange also maintained that there were no wallet private key leaks and pledged to cover all losses. 

Impact of the Binance hack

The hack soured market sentiment to ‘fear’ levels last seen in August. It dropped BTC’s value by 7% to $76.5K, before an attempted rebound. 

However, analyst Benson Sun downplayed the hack’s impact on Bitcoin, noting that it will take years to liquidate. In doing so, he drew a parallel to the Coldcard and Bitfinex hacks. 

So, the stolen BTC looks like bad news on the surface, but it’s actually a disguised form of locked-up supply.

Final Summary

  • Binance estimates total stolen funds to be $6.3B, with half of the stash now frozen.
  • Stolen $1.5B BTC won’t be sold immediately, but ETH could face more pressure.

data.title: ‘Our collateral resides off-exchange’ – Ethena downplays $8.8M Binance exposure
data.description:
Ethena, the protocol behind the synthetic, yield-generating stablecoin USDe, has downplayed exposure to the Binance hack. The team clarified that all their USDe backing resides offchain with its custodians, not on centralized exchanges. 

In fact, for the Binance scenario, the team claimed only $8.8 million in unrealized PnL (profit and loss) exposure to the platform. 

The total unrealized PNL exposure to Binance is ~$8.8M, far below the excess reserve fund of >$60m.

In a separate update following the FUD tied to the Binance exploit, Ethena added that independent attestors, Chainlink and Llama Risk, have verified its overcollateralized backing for USDe. 

Each of these independent 3rd parties mentioned above have confirmed USDe remains overcollateralised by more than $60m at >101.0%.

But before evaluating the claims, AMBCrypto explored why the community seemed worried about Ethena’s outsized exposure to the exploit. 

Ethena’s massive partnership with Binance

Ethena and Binance recently signed a partnership agreement for RWA (real-world assets) basis trade. This involves Binance’s bStocks, which promised an 11% yield and a great expansion into a $150T opportunity in the equity sector for USDe backing. 

The deal was signed last month, but the exposure seems relatively small. 

According to Ethena, RWA basis accounts for $51 million, or 1.2% of its $4.54 billion collateral for USDe. Beyond the RWA basis, Ethena also uses the crypto basis across Bitcoin [BTC] and Ethereum [ETH] to hunt for yield. The crypto basis segment accounts for about 17% of the USDe backing ($628 million) and is spread across Binance, Deribit, Coinbase, Huobi, Bybit, OKX, and Hyperliquid. 

Collectively, this is about 18% USDe collateral exposure to crypto platforms for RWA and crypto basis. In fact, the largest share of the collateral is DeFi lending ($1.3 billion) across Aave and Morpho. But Aave was also affected and paused operations after the Binance hack. So, the contagion risk fears over Ethena’s exposure to the exploit were warranted. 

However, as the project mentioned, it has off-exchange settlements (OES) or custody arrangements with Coinbase, Copper, and Ceffu. So, the risk may be limited, as the project said. 

In fact, Mikhail Kedzel, Founder of Yumi Finance, confirmed that Binance offers such off-chain arrangements to top institutional players. 

For everyone asking why: it’s because Ethena doesn’t keep funds in Binance’s hot wallet. They keep it with their custodian, and Binance just ‘recognizes’ it as funds stored at the CEX. Stuff only really available to the big guys.

It’s like the ‘custodied collateral lending’ design being explored by Aave. 

That said, the Binance attacker stole and dumped 217 million ENA ($34 million) for ETH. This dragged ENA below $0.19 after a 16% drop. Whether Ethena’s clarification on the Binance hack is enough to stop the pullback remains unclear. 

Final Summary

  • Ethena clarified that it can cover the $8.8 million Binance exposure.
  • Binance attacker sold $33 million in ENA for ETH to avoid seizure and freezing.

data.title: How did Binance hacker leverage Aave to outsmart Tether, Circle freeze?
data.description:
The Binance hacker pre-empted some of the industry’s potential reactions and planned countermeasures, including using Aave and UniswapX to avoid seizures and fund freezes. 

On Thursday, the attacker, now confirmed as North Korea’s TraderTraitor, made an initial $3.79B sweep on the Ethereum network, including 200,630 ETH and some stablecoins. 

Knowing that Tether, Circle, and other platforms would move quickly to freeze the stablecoins and other assets, the attacker deposited $60M USDT on Aave and borrowed out 19,760 WETH ($45.13M). This happened between 20:58 UTC and 21:01 UTC on Thursday, 29th October.  

Similarly, TraderTraitor swapped $325M USDT using UniswapX and Iinch between 21:34 UTC and 21:09 UTC.

In fact, analysts noticed that the hacker was forced to pay 10% of their swapped amount to fast-track the orders before freezing began. The UniswapX transfers took about 35 minutes, while Aave borrowing took only 5 minutes. Subsequently, the hacker unwrapped the WETH and got the native, unfreezable 142,062 ETH.  

Tether and Circle began the freezes by around 21:18 UTC, stopping further conversions. However, the attacker now had 420K ETH (unwrapped 142K ETH, original 200K ETH from Binance wallets, and other swapped non-USDT assets). 

Commenting on the unfortunate but massive scheme, one analyst said, 

The Binance hacker might have just pulled off one of the smartest moves I’ve seen in crypto. Tether can freeze the USDT sitting in the wallet. But it can’t freeze the ETH he already borrowed.

He added, 

So now Aave is left holding frozen collateral, while the hacker is sitting on liquid ETH.

Aave denies bad debt claims after Binance hack

Here, it’s worth noting that the KelpDAO hack leveraged a similar DeFi lending loophole to cash out and launder stolen funds. Aave was left with over $120M in bad debt. 

However, Aave founder Stani Kulechov denied that bad debt claims were applicable to the Binance hack incident. 

Actually, there is no bad debt, in fact, it’s over-collateralized with stable collateral. Kelp was different.

What remains unclear, however, is who will be repaid the $60M: Is it Binance, the primary victim, or Aave, which is also a secondary victim? 

In fact, some have even wondered how over $1M was allowed to be signed off without human review, let alone $325M swept from some of Binance’s hot wallets. For centralized exchanges such as Binance, caps make sense. However, for non-custodial decentralized platforms, it’s a different setup that is designed to have no human intervention. 

According to Chainalysis, platforms running the wallets on Ethereum with the bug that the attacker used should now be vigilant and upgrade accordingly. 

Final Summary

  • Binance hacker used Aave and UniswapX to swap $365M USDT to unfreezable +120K ETH.
  • Aave denied claims that the incident left it with bad debt like the KelpDAO exploit.

data.title: MSTR stock falls 6.8% in 2026 despite Strategy’s $20.9B Q3 income – Why?
data.description:
Michael Saylor’s Strategy has released its financial results for the third quarter of 2026.

According to the results, the largest Bitcoin [BTC] DAT reported a massive $20.91 billion operating income in Q3 2026, compared with $3.89 billion during the same quarter last year.

Here, the main catalyst behind this was the appreciation in the value of its Bitcoin holdings.  Well, to reach this milestone, the company spent approximately $14.33 billion on Bitcoin purchases during this period. Remarking on the same, Andrew Kang, Chief Financial Officer at Strategy, said,

Q3 operating income of $21 billion was the largest ever in Strategy’s history.

At the time of writing, Strategy held approximately 848,517 BTC, worth $66.48 billion, representing a 26% increase in its Bitcoin holdings since the beginning of the year.

What dragged down MSTR stock in Q3 2026?  

Despite such optimistic results, Strategy’s common stock, MSTR, was trading at $141.62 at press time after a drop of 2.44% in the past trading day. Not only that, but MSTR was also down by 6.80% in the year so far.  

Additionally, Strategy’s BTC yield also stood at negative 3.7% year-to-date. In other words, Strategy’s share dilution had outpaced Bitcoin accumulation on a per-share basis.

Hence, just increasing Bitcoin holdings was not enough for the existing shareholders to have a larger Bitcoin exposure per share. 

Q3 financial results suggest…

Notably, the firm’s total revenue declined 3% year-over-year to $125.4 million, compared with $128.7 million in Q3 2025.

On the other hand, Strategy repurchased approximately $2.04 billion worth of its preferred stock (STRC) shares during 2026, buying them at an average price of $97.39 against their stated value of $100. Furthermore, STRC reached $99.92, closing in on its $100 target price, per an October 30 report from AMBCrypto. 

Lastly, Strategy also used its capital markets to fund its Bitcoin purchases. According to reports, Strategy raised approximately $21.23 billion through capital markets during 2026, primarily through equity offerings.

In fact, during Q3, it generated approximately $5.41 billion in net proceeds through MSTR share sales. At the same time, it also sold approximately $431.8 million worth of Bitcoin year-to-date to fund preferred stock dividends and STRC repurchases.

Has MSTR lost ground in 2026?

All in all, it’s clear that though Strategy is strengthening its position as one of the world’s largest corporate Bitcoin holders, however, its earnings remain highly sensitive to Bitcoin’s price movements.

This is one of the primary reasons why MSTR is still struggling to surpass the $400 price level last seen in Q3 2025. 

MSTR’s reports, however, coincided with Bitcoin’s price surging from around $58K to $83K in Q3 2026, with the king coin changing hands at $78,501.71 at press time, down 1.9% in the past 24 hours.

Final Summary

  • Strategy’s common stock, MSTR, was trading at $141.62 at press time after a drop of 2.44% in the past trading day.
  • Strategy’s Bitcoin holdings represent a 26% increase in its Bitcoin holdings since the beginning of 2026.

data.title: ICE joins hands with Hyperliquid builder to launch U.S. perpetual futures market – Report
data.description:
Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE), is partnering with Trade[XYZ], one of the major builders of markets on decentralized exchange Hyperliquid [HYPE], to introduce a regulated perpetual futures market in the United States.

According to Bloomberg, the plan is to bring perpetual futures trading for traditional financial assets and cryptocurrencies into the U.S. market. However, this remains subject to approval from the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) agency.

This is because access to such products remains limited for U.S. investors because of regulatory restrictions.

All about the ICE-Trade [XYZ] agreement

Under the agreement, ICE and Trade[XYZ] plan to list perpetual futures linked to equities, stock market indices, commodities, foreign exchange (FX), and cryptocurrencies.

That said, the contracts would be accessible through participating brokers and trading platforms. In fact, the planned infrastructure would also include clearing systems, alongside know-your-customer (KYC) and anti-money laundering (AML) compliance measures.

At the same time, clearing (the back-end system) would help manage counterparty risk and ensure trades are processed and settled according to the applicable rules. Lastly, ICE will also make a strategic equity investment in Trade[XYZ], although the financial terms have not been disclosed yet.

Why was Hyperliquid builder a good choice, though? 

This comes as Trade[XYZ] has established a significant presence on Hyperliquid, reporting more than $650 billion in trading volume in just over a year.

Additionally, its builder-deployed markets account for roughly half of Hyperliquid’s trading activity. 

Simultaneously, the company secured a license for an S&P 500 perpetual contract in March and has also introduced products tied to assets such as crude oil and equity benchmarks.

Therefore, the partnership could bridge traditional financial markets and blockchain-based derivatives trading by combining ICE’s exchange and clearing expertise with Trade[XYZ]’s experience in decentralized markets. 

Other platforms sailing the same boat

Additionally, Payward, Kraken’s parent company, also plans to introduce on-chain perpetual futures for eligible U.S. traders through Hyperliquid, pending regulatory approval.

At the same time, Crypto.com CEO Kris Marszalek announced that the company received SEC authorization to offer tokenized stock perpetual futures in the U.S. through its new futures exchange, OG.com, following discussions with the SEC and CFTC.

Interestingly, all this followed Ark Invest questioning Hyperliquid’s ambition to become an “everything exchange,” citing limited decentralization, an anonymous team, and negligible spot trading.

Final Summary

  • With this, ICE plans to bring perpetual futures trading for traditional financial assets and cryptocurrencies into the U.S. market.
  • Trade[XYZ] has established a significant presence on Hyperliquid, reporting more than $650 billion in trading volume in just over a year.

data.title: Binance investigates potential hack as Tether freezes over 1.567B USDT
data.description:
Binance is in the news today after it announced that it was investigating reports of a “potential security issue.” The announcement followed alerts about large wallet transfers and a statement from Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino that the company had frozen more than 1.567 billion USDT.

In fact, the exchange assured customers that their funds were “completely safe.” 

Binance issues a customer warning

In its statement on X, Binance said its security teams were urgently reviewing the available information. It promised further updates through official channels once details had been verified.

Binance’s statement didn’t give a loss estimate or explanation of how the suspected incident occurred.

Tether reports a large freeze

According to Ardoino, Tether froze more than 1.567 billion USDT related to a potential Binance exchange hack. USDT is Tether’s dollar-linked stablecoin.

Freezing tokens means they cannot be moved from the offending addresses. Ardoino’s number refers to the amount handled by Tether; but at press time, the losses were still being tallied up.

For his part, Binance founder Changpeng Zhao [CZ] commended Tether for stepping in promptly. He also said that about $823 million was also frozen by Circle [USDC issuer].

CZ also that the activity looked like a hack, claiming that he expects that customer assets would be completely covered.

User funds are safe! It does look like a hack on Binance. Appreciate the quick freeze from Tether (~$971m) and Circle (~$823m). I don’t manage Binance (.com) anymore, but as a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered.

Blockaid examines transfers across several networks

Blockaid, a security firm, picked up on large outgoings in other wallets to and from Binance-owned wallets, which began at about 20:24 UTC on 29th October.

It first looked at Ethereum, Arbitrum, and Avalanche, with related receipts on Optimism. Blockaid claimed these were all consistent with being fraudulent, but admitted it could also be an internal money transfer.

The firm’s preliminary estimates included about $2.5 billion from two Ethereum wallets, plus 780 million USDC from another account. Those amounts were still being reconciled, and at the time of this writing, the estimate was over $5 billion. 

In a follow-up, Blockaid said one examined account had been configured to let a designated operator drain its assets.

Observers will be waiting for Binance’s follow-up communication to verify their affected systems, the scope of the attack, and the impact on their customers.

Final Summary

  • Binance is investigating a potential security issue, with the exchange claiming that customer funds are safe.
  • Ardoino announced Tether froze over 1.567 billion USDT as the cause and final losses remain unresolved.
